title: Christ's veiled answer to spare sincere followers
english: So then, so that he would not seem in some way to grieve his sincere followers by having refused the explanation they wanted to learn, he says in a veiled way, “But about that day or hour no one knows, not even the angels, nor the son, but only the Father” (Matthew 24:36).
translator_notes: The Greek text is a fragment, beginning mid-sentence and ending mid-sentence: ...μαθεῖν, δόξῃ πως λυπεῖν τοὺς γνησιεύοντας, ἐπεσκιασμένως φησί 'Περὶ δὲ τῆς ἡμέρας ἐκείνης ἢ τῆς ὥρας, οὐδεὶς οἶδεν, οὐδὲ 'οἱ ἄγγελοι, οὐδὲ ὁ υἱὸς, εἰ μὴ ὁ...
baehrens: PG 76; Fragmenta contra Diodorum frag rem early
orientation: Cyril is explaining why Christ, when asked about the day and hour, spoke in a veiled way rather than refusing outright.

title: The veiled saying means even an adopted son must not seek what is beyond nature
english: He said that only the Father knows. Understand it this way: even if a human being has been called to adoption and has been shown to be a new son, he must not seek what is beyond nature, nor think it right to learn what not even [text breaks off]
translator_notes: Copy-text: PG 76; Fragmenta contra Diodorum via Khazarzar (Fragmenta ex libro contra Diodorum Tarsensem.pdf).
True OET; Pass A ≠ Pass B. Condensed lemma-led tip.
No copyrighted English base. Melito skipped; never Cyril Matthew densify; skip Pusey-PD / Greystone / Lunn / Hill.
Skip Collectio dictorum florilegium; skip ascriptus De sancta trinitate.
baehrens: PG 76; Fragmenta contra Diodorum frag rem mid
orientation: Cyril is explaining the veiled force of Christ's saying from Matthew 24:36, addressing what the disciples should understand from it.

title: No human will know what even angels do not know
english: The Father has not revealed it to the angels. And if an angel does not know, neither will a human being know, even if he has been called to adoption.
translator_notes: Copy-text: PG 76; Fragmenta contra Diodorum via Khazarzar (Fragmenta ex libro contra Diodorum Tarsensem.pdf).

baehrens: PG 76; Fragmenta contra Diodorum frag rem close
orientation: Cyril is closing his explanation of Christ's saying that no one knows the day or hour, arguing that since the Father has not revealed it even to angels, no human being will know it, even if called to adoption.
